page.title: Ad blocker
page.description: Blocks ads, trackers and malware for every device on your network.

install.title: Ad blocker is not installed
install.body: Install it to block ads, trackers and malware on every device that uses your network. Installing starts nothing; you turn the blocker on afterwards.

status.title: Status
status.stale: The DNS server runs older settings than these, from before a clock change or an update.

off.label: Turned off
off.body: The blocker is off. Turn it on to start a DNS server on this machine at {address}.

portTaken.label: Port in use
portTaken.body: Another DNS server already answers on port 53 at {address}, so the blocker cannot start there. Turn that one off, then retry.

starting.label: Starting
starting.body: The DNS server is starting at {address}. The first blocklists can take a minute to download.

stalled.label: Not starting
stalled.body: The DNS server at {address} has not answered for a minute. It may be failing to start with these settings. Try again, or turn it off.

portHeld.label: Could not start
portHeld.body: The DNS server could not start at {address}. Another program on this machine may be using port 53, or a download failed. Nothing on your network changed. Try again.

conflict.label: Not answering
conflict.body: Something other than the blocker answers on port 53 at {address}. Retry to start the blocker again.

blocking.label: Blocking
blocking.body: Blocking at {address}. Devices that use this address as their DNS server are protected.

noAddress.label: No address
noAddress.body: This machine has no address on your network that Polaris knows of yet, so there is nothing to point devices at. Check again in a minute.

router.title: Point your network at it
router.intro: Devices use the blocker once your router hands out its address as the DNS server.
router.step1: Open your router's settings page and find the DHCP or LAN settings.
router.step2: Set the primary DNS server to {address}.
router.step3: Leave the secondary DNS server empty. Devices use it whenever they like, and it would let ads through.
router.step4: Save, then reconnect your devices or wait for them to renew their address.

lists.title: Lists to block
lists.intro: Lists are downloaded again on the schedule below. More lists block more, and break more sites.

rules.title: Your rules
rules.intro: One per line: a name, *.name for everything under it, or /regex/. Allowed names win over every list.

upstream.title: Resolver
upstream.intro: Where allowed names are looked up. The encrypted ones keep your lookups private from your provider.

records.title: Local names
records.intro: Names your network answers itself, like nas.home.
records.name: Name

validation.invalidUrl: Enter an http or https address.
validation.refresh: Enter a whole number from 1 to 168.
validation.aliasClash: These names are both an alias and a local name: {names}. Keep one.
validation.invalidClient: Not an address, a range or a device name:
validation.invalidDeviceName: Letters, digits, dots and dashes; no spaces.
validation.timePair: Set both times, or neither for the whole day.
validation.sameTime: The start and the end cannot be the same time.
validation.cacheRange: The least time cannot be more than the most.

errors.notInstalled: Ad blocker is not installed. Install it from the Marketplace first.
errors.tooLarge: These rules are too long to apply. Remove some of your own rules and save again.
errors.noAddress: This machine has no address on your network yet. Check again in a minute.
errors.portTaken: Another DNS server already answers on port 53 here. Turn it off, then retry.
errors.portBusy: Another program on this machine already uses port 53, so the DNS server cannot start. Stop it, then retry.
errors.notApplied: Your settings are saved, but the DNS server did not start with them. See the status above and try again.
errors.invalid: Some values are not valid. Fix the marked fields and save again.
errors.generic: That did not work. Try again in a moment.
errors.notRunning: The DNS server is not running. Turn blocking on first.
errors.notAnswering: The DNS server did not answer. Wait a moment and try again.
errors.servicesOffline: Could not download the services' domains, so nothing was saved. Check this machine's internet connection and save again.
errors.servicesMissing: Some services are no longer in the public list, so nothing was saved. Turn them off and save again.

insights.title: Activity
insights.empty: No lookups yet today. Once the router hands out this DNS server, they show up here.
insights.pausedFor: Blocking paused, back on in {minutes} min
insights.logOff: The DNS server is running settings from before the query log, so lookups are not recorded yet. Apply them to start recording.
insights.rangeKept: Only {days} days are kept. Keep more under History below.
insights.nowAllowed: {domain} is now allowed. The DNS server restarts to apply it.
insights.nowBlocked: {domain} is now blocked. The DNS server restarts to apply it.
insights.metricsOff: Apply the settings once to count the names on your lists.
insights.liveHint: The newest lookups today, read again every few seconds.
insights.listsRefreshing: The lists are downloading again. Counts update when they finish.
insights.listsFailed: {count} list downloads failed since the DNS server started. Check that each list address still works.
insights.listsPerCategory: Counted per category: the DNS server reports each category's lists together, not list by list.

aliases.title: Aliases (CNAME)
aliases.intro: A name that answers with another name, like media.home pointing at nas.home.
aliases.name: Alias

groups.title: Device groups
groups.intro: Some devices can block other categories than the rest of the network. A device in no group uses the lists above.
groups.empty: No groups. Every device uses the lists above.
groups.name: Group name
groups.clients: Devices: an address, a range or a name, one per line

history.title: History and device names
history.namesFromHint: Its address. Devices then show by name instead of address. Leave empty to show addresses.

routerGuide.signIn: Open the router's settings page and sign in.
routerGuide.relay: Go to {path}, choose {field} and enter as the primary server
routerGuide.ipv6: If your network uses IPv6, go to {path} and put in {field}
routerGuide.conflict: Go to {path} and turn off {field}. While it is on, the router sends devices to its own DNS and skips this one.
routerGuide.relayNote: This router keeps handing out its own address and asks the blocker on behalf of every device. Ads are still blocked, but every lookup shows up as coming from the router.

notes.fritzbox: For IPv6, also tick "Also announce DNSv6 server via router advertisement (RFC 5006)". Afterwards fritz.box may stop opening on your devices; use 192.168.178.1 instead.
notes.tplink: On a Deco, the same field is in the app under More > Advanced > DHCP Server. Restart the main Deco after saving.
notes.unifi: Devices pick it up when their lease renews, usually within a day. Turning a device off and on again is quicker.
notes.netgear: Devices keep the router as their DNS server, so nothing changes on them and no reconnect is needed.
notes.zte: Some provider builds lock this page or quietly undo the change; if no device shows up below, ask your provider to set it. If phones still show ads, they get the provider's DNS over IPv6: ask your provider to turn IPv6 off.
notes.eero: Custom DNS is greyed out while any eero Plus filter is on: turn those off first. Saving restarts the network.
notes.googlewifi: If the network stops loading pages after saving, a phone on mobile data can still open the app and put the DNS back.

check.title: Are devices using it?
check.failed: Polaris could not read the log just now. Check again in a moment.
check.none: No device has asked the blocker anything in the last 24 hours. The router is still handing out another DNS server, or devices have not renewed their address yet.
check.routerOnly: Only the router ({router}) is asking the blocker. Devices go through the router, so they are covered, but the blocker cannot tell them apart. Set the DHCP DNS server above to see each device.
check.relayed: The router ({router}) is asking the blocker for your devices, as expected for this router. Ads are being blocked.
check.devices: {count, plural, one {One device has} other {# devices have}} used the blocker in the last 24 hours:
check.logOff: The blocker is not keeping a log yet, so Polaris cannot see which devices use it. Apply the settings below once and check again.

devices.title: Device names
devices.intro: Name a device by its address. The log shows the name, and a group can hold it.
devices.empty: No names yet. Devices show by address, or by the name your router gives them.
devices.name: Device name

forwards.title: Local domains
forwards.intro: Send a domain to another server, like your router for home.lan or a reverse zone.
forwards.empty: None. Every name goes to the resolvers above.

safe.title: Safe search filters
safe.intro: For every device on the network. A browser setting cannot turn it off.
safe.search: Filter explicit results on Google and Bing

schedules.title: Schedules
schedules.intro: Lists that block only at set hours, for every device. Outside those hours they let everything through.
schedules.empty: No schedules. Every list that is on blocks all day.
schedules.noLists: Turn on a list above to schedule it.

services.title: Blocked services
services.intro: Block an app or site by name for every device, or only for a device group. Its domains are downloaded from AdGuard's public list when you save.

log.off: Lookups show up here once blocking is on.

engine.title: Engine
engine.intro: How the blocker answers, beyond what it blocks.
engine.cacheHint: 0 keeps each answer as long as its own time to live.
engine.prefetch: Ask again early for popular names
engine.dropTypesHint: AAAA leaves devices on IPv4 only; HTTPS and ANY are rarely needed.
engine.fqdnOnly: Answer names without a dot as not found
engine.dnssec: Check the DNSSEC signature of each answer

lookup.title: Is this name blocked?
lookup.intro: Ask the blocker about one name, as a device with no group of its own would.
lookup.invalid: Type one name, like ads.example.com, with no * or /.

network.title: Seen on the network
network.intro: Every device that asked the blocker. Open one to see its lookups.
network.empty: No device has asked in this range.
network.name: Name it
